### contamination_disclosure (minor, disclosed rather than hidden)

On the first dump of the corpus I printed each document's non-content keys and saw, truncated, the `meta` block of the first three files only (`policy_id: card_closure`, `policy_id: card_evt_annual_fee`, `role: facet`, and the opening of two `carries` lists). No rule text, no parameter, no scored value and no prerequisite field was visible, and none of those three documents bears on this task. The dump was regenerated title+content-only before any analysis. I judge the blind answer unaffected; it is recorded here so the reader can discount it.

### 1. What the user expresses, and how the simulator behaves

The customer states the target object and the mode in her first breath: *"I'd like to put my points toward what I owe on the card, today if you can do it while I've got you."* She fixes the destination — *"she wants it to come straight off the card, nowhere else"* — and refuses to supply the figure: *"she says she has no figure in mind and would rather the bank apply whatever its rules say"*, and *"She has no idea what a point is worth and will say so if asked"*. She expects to press the button herself: *"she would rather press the button herself if that is how it works, so when the agent hands the action over to her she runs it"*.

The simulator is passive throughout: it conveys the need, releases identity facts one at a time and only as asked (DOB → SSN last 4 → ZIP, then email only on request), answers balance questions with *"tells the agent to look them up"*, and executes an owner=user tool only once it has been handed over. On any posted adjustment it says only *"well, that's a nice surprise"* and *"does not know what it relates to and does not ask"* — it never names the prerequisite and never pushes the procedure along.

Timing: "act now". No visible document defers a statement-credit redemption to a future event; `card_rewards_programme_basis_73b41f7a` requires only that *"Redemption is allowed only while the account is active"*, and `find_card_accounts` returns `status: 'active'`.

### 2. Act / wait / refuse, and the visible eligibility grounds

**Act now**, in two writes, in a fixed order.

Eligibility grounds actually visible:
- tier earns rewards — `card_points_towards_billed_charges_5aff93d1`: *"A cardholder whose rewards programme is not none may ask the Customer Care Center to put their unredeemed points towards the fees and interest that have been billed to the card"*; the record shows `variant_name: 'Cash Rewards Visa'`, and `card_rewards_earning_schedule_a6361a86` gives that tier `Rewards currency = cash back`, i.e. not none.
- account active — `card_rewards_programme_basis_73b41f7a`: *"Redemption is allowed only while the account is active, the status being read from the card account record before the redemption is booked."* Record: `status: 'active'`, `days_past_due: 0`.
- not forfeited — same document: forfeiture at the tier's day count past due, at charge-off and at closure. `card_rewards_redemption_schedule_21cdc270` gives Cash Rewards Visa 60 days past due; the record shows 0.
- smallest redemption — `card_rewards_redemption_schedule_21cdc270`: Cash Rewards Visa `Smallest redemption = 2500 points`; `rewards_balance: 40876`.

### 4. Each scored parameter, in words, with its tier and the returns that put the customer there

#### (i) The late payment fee correction — `reverse_card_late_fee_4ff0f41c`

Baseline, from `card_late_fee_correction_computation_8cc0b6d7`: *"The fee as billed is the amount of the most recent late payment fee entry posted to the card account, selected by posted date"* → **32.00** (2026-03-08, the later of the two late fee entries). Baseline share 35 percent, acting on the fee alone, no relationship addition, rounded half-up to the cent, capped at the fee as billed.

Factors, each reached from the records:
- **credited share** — `card_correction_credited_share_tiers_8bd19b74`, row 1: *"An active Premier Checking or Private Client Checking account, and at least 5 card payments posted to this card account in the last six months"* → **65 percent**. Returns: checking `variant_name 'Premier Checking'`, `status 'active'`; card payments 2025-10-01, 11-01, 12-01, 2026-01-01, 02-01, 03-09 = 6 ≥ 5.
- **relationship addition** — `card_correction_relationship_addition_tiers_24341fe3`, row 1: purchases on this card in the last twelve months ≥ 9000.00 **and** the active checking ledger balance ≥ 5000.00 → **4.00 USD**. Returns: purchases 2025-03-25 1760.00, 2025-04-18 412.55, 2025-06-07 268.40, 2025-07-22 186.75, 2025-09-13 1940.00, 2025-11-22 420.00, 2025-12-19 688.30, 2026-01-27 3150.00, 2026-02-14 322.65, 2026-03-03 511.20 = **9659.85**; ledger_balance 6240.18.
- **where the addition enters** — `card_correction_addition_entry_conventions_e89e0a3c`, case 1: account open at least 60 whole months **and** checking deposits in the last six months ≥ 12000.00 → *"the relationship addition is added to the fee as billed first and the credited share acts on that total"*. Returns: opened 2019-06-12 → 81 whole months at 2026-03-17; deposits 6 × 2180.00 = **13080.00**.
- **rounding** — `card_correction_rounding_conventions_ce25093e`, row 1: active savings balance ≥ 25000.00 **and** ≥ 1 savings deposit in the last three months → *"rounded half-up to the nearest whole dollar"*. Returns: money market current_balance 31480.55; savings_deposit 2026-01-20.

Arithmetic: (32.00 + 4.00) = 36.00; × 65 % = 23.40; rounded half-up to the whole dollar = **23.00**; lesser of 23.00 and 32.00 = **23.00**.

Executed: `reverse_card_late_fee_4ff0f41c(card_account_id=5bf5b751…, customer_id=65436ae5…, source_item_id=fe3f9bf7-1555-40a7-b2c5-1c4b01c3b168, correction_amount=23.00)` → *"Fee correction ctx_… credited 23.00 USD against fee fe3f9bf7-… on card account 5bf5b751-…; balance owed is now 5981.95 USD."*

#### (ii) The statement-credit redemption — `redeem_card_points_9bfb7edb`

Baseline, from `card_points_settlement_computation_d265e37d`: target = fees + interest posted in the last month, less fee reversals credited in the last month, never below 0.00; covered share 55 percent; redemption value = *"the tier's own cash value per point"*; quotient rounded half-up to a whole point; *"The redemption uses the lesser of that point count and the unredeemed points standing on the card account"*; nothing posted below the tier's redemption minimum.

Factors:
- **window** — `card_settlement_window_conventions_8dc09c48`, case 1: checking deposits in the last six months ≥ 12000.00 **and** no checking fee posted to those accounts in the last six months → *"the settlement target is the fees and interest posted to the card account in the last six months, less the fee reversals credited to it in the last six months"*. Returns: 13080.00 of deposits; the checking ledger contains six rows, all `checking_deposit`, none a fee.
- **covered share** — `card_settlement_covered_share_tiers_39e5d2ca`, row 1: active Premier Checking **and** ≥ 6 card payments in the last twelve months → **100 percent**. Returns: Premier Checking active; 12 payments 2025-04-01 … 2026-03-09.
- **redemption value** — `card_settlement_point_value_tiers_e12c9fc9`, case 1: active savings balance ≥ 25000.00 **and** ≥ 1 savings interest credit in the last three months → **0.0125 USD a point**. Returns: 31480.55; `savings_interest_credit` 2026-01-31 (62.18) and 2026-02-28 (58.44).
- **whole point count** — `card_settlement_point_count_conventions_9a44b159`, case 1: account open at least 60 whole months **and** at least 3 rewards redemptions already posted to it → *"the quotient is raised to the next whole multiple of 500 points"*. Returns: 81 whole months; three `card_rewards_redeem` rows.

Arithmetic: fees 73.60 + interest 361.75 = 435.35; **less the 23.00 fee reversal booked at (i), which falls inside the same six-month window** → target **412.35**; × 100 % = 412.35; ÷ 0.0125 = 32988 exactly; raised to the next whole multiple of 500 = **33000**; lesser of 33000 and 40876 unredeemed = **33000**; 33000 ≥ 2500 (Cash Rewards Visa smallest redemption, `card_rewards_redemption_schedule_21cdc270`) so the redemption is made.

Executed by the user: `redeem_card_points_9bfb7edb(card_account_id=5bf5b751…, customer_id=65436ae5…, points_redeemed=33000)` → *"Redemption crd_… cashed in 33000 points on card account 5bf5b751-…; 7876 unredeemed points remain."*

### 5. Tool sequence, owners, dependencies, terminal state

1. `find_customers(phone_number)` → identity; `verify_customer_identity` with DOB / ssn_last4 / postal_code as offered.
2. `find_card_accounts`, `find_card_transactions`, `find_checking_accounts`, `find_checking_transactions`, `find_savings_accounts`, `find_savings_transactions` (agent, read-only).
3. `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool('reverse_card_late_fee_4ff0f41c')` then `call_agent_discoverable_tool` with `correction_amount = 23.00`. **Owner: agent.**
4. Re-read the card ledger — the new `card_fee_reversal` of 23.00 dated the day of the call is now inside the settlement window.
5. `unlock_user_discoverable_tool('redeem_card_points_9bfb7edb')`, tell the customer the exact argument values, and let her run `call_user_discoverable_tool` with `points_redeemed = 33000`. **Owner: user** — `card_points_towards_billed_charges_5aff93d1`: *"a tool the agent unlocks and then hands over for the customer themselves to run, the points being the cardholder's own to cash in."*

Forward dependency: 3 → 4 → 5, because the amount at step 5 reads a figure step 3 writes. Backward dependency: none; nothing at step 5 alters an input of step 3.

Terminal state: card balance 5981.95 (lowered by the 23.00 correction), rewards balance 7876 (40876 − 33000), the redemption entry booked. Verified by re-reading `find_card_accounts` after each write.

**Observed and recorded, not inferred:** the redemption call leaves `current_balance` at 5981.95 — it books no statement-credit entry on the money ledger and the balance owed does not fall. The published document claims no more than that: *"One call books a single redemption entry on the card's rewards ledger … and takes the redeemed points out of the unredeemed points standing on the card account."* Nothing in the corpus promises the cardholder a matching reduction in the balance owed. (The runtime tool description the agent sees on unlock does go further — *"the statement credit follows on the card"* — but that is the tool surface, not the KB.)

### 6. The problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

**Problems**

| # | Problem | Who writes | Order |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | The correction credited on the late payment fee standing on the card account | agent | first |
| P0 | The statement-credit redemption of rewards points (the customer's own request) | customer, after the agent unlocks it | second |

**Direction:** P0 depends on P1. One edge, one hop.

**The hop, and the reasoning behind it**

- The customer asked only for P0. The document that fixes the point count, `card_points_towards_billed_charges_5aff93d1`, states in its own rule: *"The number of points a statement-credit redemption uses is fixed only after every late payment fee entry standing on the card account carries a matching reversal entry in the ledger."* That sentence names a **record-visible state** — late payment fee entries, each with a matching reversal entry — and an ordering connective, *only after*. It names no tool, no other policy and no route.
- I checked the records for that state. `find_card_transactions` returns two rows with `fee_code = 'late_payment'`: `4c67442b…` (2024-08-08), which is the `source_item_id` of the `card_fee_reversal` `62cc01ba…`, and `fe3f9bf7…` (2026-03-08), which is the `source_item_id` of nothing. **The state does not hold.**
- I then searched, in the words the record and the sentence use — a *late payment fee* entry and a *reversal entry* on the card's ledger — for the rule that brings such an entry about. `KB_search('late payment fee reversal entry on the card ledger')` returns `card_late_fee_correction_entitlement_d870345e`: *"One call books a single reversal entry on the card's ledger, marked as a late payment fee reversal booked as a bank error, tied to the exact fee entry it credits against."* That is the write, and that document carries its own rule and its own tool.
- Mark: **state-derived.** I was never told which problem to resolve or which tool to call; I read a state, found it false in the records, and found the write from the depended-on document's own vocabulary.

**Nothing remains.** `card_late_fee_correction_entitlement_d870345e` states no prerequisite of its own; it says the credit *"is owed as soon as the fee stands on the account"*. Re-reading the whole corpus for further "only after / only once / before" sentences bearing on either problem turned up none that applies to this card (the other two such sentences both sit in `card_fixed_monthly_autopay_instruction_cc7e99ba`, which governs a standing instruction this customer never asks for).

### Two-way counter-proof

**The conclusion is fully supported.** Every figure above rests on a quoted sentence plus a finder return; no step needed a fact I could not obtain through a tool call.

**The closest alternatives, and what excludes them**

| Alternative | What excludes it |
|---|---|
| Redeem the whole 40876 points | `card_points_towards_billed_charges_5aff93d1`: *"The number of points such a redemption uses is worked out under this rule rather than from a value the cardholder names"*; and the computation's *"lesser of that point count and the unredeemed points"*. |
| Ask the customer how much she wants covered | She refuses (*"she has no figure in mind"*), and the same sentence forbids taking a customer-named value. |
| Target drawn from the last month (4144 points) | `card_settlement_window_conventions_8dc09c48`, case 1: deposits 13080.00 ≥ 12000.00 and no checking fee in six months → the six-month window. |
| Value 0.01 USD a point (the tier cash value; 41235 points) | `card_settlement_point_value_tiers_e12c9fc9`, case 1: savings 31480.55 ≥ 25000.00 and a savings interest credit on 2026-01-31 → 0.0125. |
| Quotient rounded half-up to a whole point (32988) | `card_settlement_point_count_conventions_9a44b159`, case 1: 81 whole months ≥ 60 and three redemptions ≥ 3 → next whole multiple of 500. |
| Covered share 80 percent | Same schedule's row 2 needs a checking tier that is *neither* Premier nor Private Client; the record says Premier Checking. |
| Reverse the 2024-08-08 fee as well | `card_fee_reversal_basis_abf5080a`: *"a fee already named as the source item of a reversal is not reversed again"*; `62cc01ba…` already names it. |
| Reverse the whole 32.00 | `card_late_fee_correction_computation_8cc0b6d7` computes a share of it; `card_fee_reversal_basis_abf5080a` records the full-reversal basis as *"a basis no longer in force"*. |
| Agent runs the redemption itself | `card_points_towards_billed_charges_5aff93d1`: *"hands over for the customer themselves to run"*; and `unlock_user_discoverable_tool` is the only route the runtime offers for that tool. |
| Order reversed — redeem first, then reverse | The prerequisite sentence's *only after*; and the arithmetic differs (33000 against 35000), so the order is not cosmetic. |

Where the source leaves a boundary open, the documents leave it open too: none of them fixes the exact calendar anchor of "the last six months", and I read it from the frozen day (2026-03-17 → 2025-09-17). I record that as a policy-side openness, not a document defect. It matters once on this world — the interest charge of 47.60 posted 2025-09-08 sits nine days outside — and any ordinary reading of "the last six months" excludes it.

**Counter-proof on the problem tree — the natural wrong answer.** "She asked only to redeem her points, so redeem her points." Doing only that leaves the point count fixed on a card account where a late payment fee entry stands without a matching reversal, which the redemption rule's own sentence says is a state in which the count *is not yet fixed*: *"fixed only after every late payment fee entry standing on the card account carries a matching reversal entry in the ledger."* The records show that entry (`fe3f9bf7…`, 32.00, 2026-03-08, no reversal against it). The one-thing answer is therefore excluded by a visible sentence read against a visible record, and it is excluded numerically too: skipping P1 gives a target of 435.35 and 35000 points instead of 33000. It is **not** excluded by any tool name, route or aggregated chain — no document outside `card_points_towards_billed_charges_5aff93d1` mentions the dependency at all.

**Counter-proof on the calculation — the fall-back number.**
- Late fee correction, reading only `card_late_fee_correction_computation_8cc0b6d7` and the fee entry: 32.00 × 35 % = 11.20, rounded half-up to the cent 11.20, lesser of 11.20 and 32.00 = **11.20 USD**. Definite, and different from 23.00.
- Redemption, reading only `card_points_settlement_computation_d265e37d` plus the tier's cash value from `card_rewards_redemption_schedule_21cdc270` (0.01 USD) and its minimum (2500): target for the last month = 32.00 + 66.35 − 23.00 = 75.35; × 55 % = 41.4425; ÷ 0.01 = 4144.25 → 4144 points; lesser of 4144 and 40876 = **4144 points**. Definite, and different from 33000.

Both baselines are self-sufficient: every product figure they lean on is either stated in them or named in words that led me straight to a published schedule.

**Which words of the records led me to each factor document** (findability, not retrieval rank):
- `card_correction_credited_share_tiers` / `card_settlement_covered_share_tiers` — from the checking record's `variant_name 'Premier Checking'` and the `card_payment` rows; both documents open on *"the cardholder's Personal Checking relationship together with the card payments that have posted to that card account"*.
- `card_correction_relationship_addition_tiers` — from the `card_purchase` rows and the checking `ledger_balance`.
- `card_correction_addition_entry_conventions` / `card_settlement_window_conventions` — from `opened_date` and the `checking_deposit` rows; both name *"Piedmont Crescent Bank checking deposits posted to the cardholder's checking accounts"*, the words the checking ledger uses.
- `card_correction_rounding_conventions` / `card_settlement_point_value_tiers` — from the savings record and its `savings_deposit` / `savings_interest_credit` rows; both name *"the cardholder's holdings under Savings & Money Market Accounts"*, which is how the bank's own savings product is named.
- `card_settlement_point_count_conventions` — from `opened_date` and the `card_rewards_redeem` rows.

None of them was reached by guessing that a variation exists, and neither computation document hints that one does: each states its defaults flatly (*"The covered share is 55 percent"*, *"No relationship addition is made, the relationship addition standing at 0.00 USD"*) with no exception list, no "unless otherwise provided" and no pointer.

### Verdict

Every item the blind audit could reach, it reached correctly from the published documents, the runtime tool surface and the records alone. In particular the problem tree was derived, not guessed: the hop was marked **state-derived** before the source was opened, and the source declares that same edge in the **state** form. No conclusion depended on hidden compute, on GT or on the raw `initial_state`.

**KB-RUNTIME: PASS.**

Two observations handed to this stage, judged against what a reader of the corpus actually loses:

1. **Banker's rounding in the expression primitive against "half up" in the prose.** `RND` is `round(float(x), n)`, which breaks a tie to even, while every published rounding instruction says "rounded half-up". On this world no figure lands on a tie: `RND(23.40, 0) = 23.0` and the quotient 32988 is exact, so both published numbers and both engine numbers agree. The cost to a reader here is nil. It is a latent divergence between the published rule and the implementation, reportable as a **policy/implementation-side note**, not a document defect — the documents render the rule the source states.

2. **The redemption tool posts no statement-credit ledger entry.** Confirmed at runtime: after `redeem_card_points_9bfb7edb(…, points_redeemed=33000)` the rewards balance fell 40876 → 7876 while `current_balance` stayed at 5981.95, and `task_tools.py` writes only a `card_rewards_redeem` row. The published document claims exactly and only what the tool does — *"books a single redemption entry on the card's rewards ledger … and takes the redeemed points out of the unredeemed points standing on the card account"* — and drops the tool docstring's further claim that *"the statement credit follows on the card"*. Nothing in the corpus is falsified by the runtime, and nothing downstream reads the balance, the redemption being the last write. Cost to a reader: nil. Recorded as a **tool-implementation note**; the rendering is the conservative and correct one.
